en: The Special Ritual Manual for the Miraculous Dhāraṇī of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of Abundant Treasures, from the North;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Court Official of the Third Rank and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Great One of Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed all sentient beings, saying:
"O sons of noble family, within the five turbidities of this evil world in Jambudvīpa in the south..."
Whether they be ordained bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
or lay upāsakas and upāsikās,
all are together within the Dharma.
I shall lead all the devas and benevolent spirits to protect this person.
For those who hear my name or know me,
I will remain by their side.
Just as one would protect the pupils of one's eyes,
or just as one would protect one's own life so that no evil beings may cause disturbance,
so it is for all men and women.
They serve me as a king;
I serve them as a king.
They serve me with all things that are noble and superior.
If they serve me with all things that are noble and excellent, I shall serve them with all things that are noble and excellent.
If they serve me with wealth, pleasure, and sounds, I shall serve them with all wealth, pleasure, and sounds.
If there is anyone who can receive, uphold, and recite this dhāraṇī as well as the methods for binding mudrās, [I shall likewise serve them].
To all who perform acts of worship before my image,
I shall comply with everything you seek;
I shall fulfill your aspirations according to your wishes.
If there are renunciants who receive and uphold [this],
I shall assist them as a youth.
If there are kings, ministers, and their subjects who receive, uphold, and make offerings to me, I shall likewise assist them.
"I shall always aspire to wealth, nobility, military might, and the royal throne, and I vow never to turn my back on them.
Good son, this is the Dharma of Mantra;
I offer it before the Buddha to the World-Honored One."
I shall protect and sustain the bhikṣus of the final dharma, the Buddha’s disciples, and all sentient beings.
Should there be anyone who harbors an evil mind toward my disciples of the final dharma, O World-Honored One, [may they be subdued].
I myself lead a vast multitude of spirits, yakṣas, gandharvas, and other beings;
I shall crush evil persons into fine dust.
Noble son, if there are those within my Dharma who constantly make offerings and receive and uphold it according to the teachings, [I shall protect them].
I shall grant you whatever you require and whatever you wish for.
If there is anyone who is able to receive and uphold my mantra-dharma,
they should first construct a mandala measuring four cubits.
In a clean room, dig out the poor soil to a depth of one foot;
then fetch pure yellow earth from a distant location.
Fill it in until it is level and even,
and construct a flight of steps one span high.
The upper level is three feet square and one span high;
it has four gates.
Place a water jar filled with scented water,
four arrows, four swords, and four mirrors on the four sides;
provide twelve platters for the offerings of food and drink.
There were four lamps of fried cakes, curd, and ghee, along with scattered flowers.
In spring and summer, various wild flowers were gathered;
in autumn and winter, colored paper flowers were scattered.
On the lower tier of the altar, mountains and rocks are painted;
on the upper tier, a large lotus flower is painted;
and in the four corners, the ocean waters are painted.
Install the image upon a lotus flower at the center;
above it, suspend sixteen banners,
all fashioned in the likeness of divine forms.
The image faces south.
The practitioner faces north toward the image and sits to recite the mantra.
The mantra for constructing the maṇḍala is as follows:
Oṃ nanda nanda naṭi naṭi nanda vāri saṃhā | If there is one who upholds this mantra-dharma...
When constructing the altar,
first recite this mantra one hundred and eight times to consecrate the ground and the site consisting of earth and stones.
All species of insects and ants will all move away and no longer dwell there;
that ground will immediately become pure.
It is fit to establish a mandala.
When binding the mandala,
strictly perform the empowerment and the delimitation of the boundary.
To form the earth-element mudrā (*pṛthivī-dhātu-mudrā*), place the right middle finger between the left index finger with its tip pointing outward;
likewise, place the right ring finger between the left little finger in the same manner.
Insert the left middle finger inward between the right index fingers so that its tip emerges toward the inside;
likewise, place the left ring finger between the right little fingers in the same manner.
The two little fingers and the index fingers are held upright and joined;
the two thumbs are also joined with their tips pointing downward.
With the thumbs joined at the base, they rest upon the ground, while the elbows support the two upper arms.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra vajri bhūruṇḍa pūrṇadha pūrṇadha hūṃ phaṭ. This mudrā can eliminate all malevolent beings within the earth.
Reaching down to the adamantine base,
it expels all evil spirits and ghosts;
one must empower it seven times while supporting the earth and sky from top to bottom.
It cannot cause harm;
one obtains pure merit.
Next, perform the mudrā for binding the boundary of the four directions.
Following the previous ritual for the boundary-marking cord,
change only this: extend the two thumbs and space them two inches apart.
Point the fingers straight upward toward the body.
Point the index finger angrily toward the right and turn.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarasara vajraprakāra hūṃ phaṭ. This mudrā can eliminate malevolent spirits, demons, and deities from the four directions.
At the site of the ritual mandala, perform the mudrās and recite the mantra seven times,
turning toward the four directions in accordance with the movement of the sun.
All yakṣas and bhūtas will retreat and disperse;
one shall attain the accomplishment of the Dharma.
Next, bind the mudrā of the space realm.
Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā,
change only this: place both thumbs so that they each rest against the side of the index fingers.
Then, point [the mudrā] toward the head and rotate it three times to the right.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vi-spra-nara-kṣa-va-jra-phaṭ ja-ra-ra-hūṃ phaṭ. This seal-mudrā can eliminate all malevolent spirits, ghosts, and deities from the air up to the peak of existence (bhavāgra).
Not daring to harbor evil thoughts,
perform the mudrā by circling it three times clockwise above the head,
empowering it with the mantra.
The flying yakṣas will retreat and disperse.
If one is able to perform the rite for accomplishing the Great Maṇḍala throughout one’s entire life,
when selecting the site before it has been measured out:
Recite the mantra once.
Bind the ground as a boundary so that it is level, firm, and solid.
Offer incense and flowers as an offering.
Furthermore, recite the mantra once more to bind the boundary of the ground.
If one erects pillars, draws the perimeter lines,
hangs banners, bells, and ornaments, and offers even a small amount of flowers, it constitutes further worship.
Recite the mantra once to establish the boundary,
arrange the colored powders for the seats,
and open out the various positions of the mandala ground.
Furthermore, recite the mantra once to perform the boundary-binding (sīmābandha).
Place the lamp upon the mandala.
Again, recite the mantra once to perform the boundary-binding.
All offering materials—such as water jars, flowers, incense, food, ghee, honey, sesame seeds, parched grain, and non-glutinous rice—should be brought into the maṇḍala.
Once they have been arranged, recite the mantra once more to perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Request the Buddha, Prajñāpāramitā, the Bodhisattvas, the Vajradevatās, and so forth.
Before making the request,
recite the mantra once more to perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
For each boundary, hold a vajra in the left hand to subdue all [obstacles],
and hold an incense burner in the right hand.
Verbally invite all the assemblies of noble ones and celestial kings;
circumambulate them three times to the right to perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Visualize the mental markers for distances such as ten thousand *li*, one thousand *li*, one hundred *li*, or one *yojana*.
In all cases, one should maintain this visualization in the mind and recite aloud: "Each of the four directions has a boundary of three *li*.
Then, one should perform offerings while maintaining the majestic deportment of movement and stillness, fully embodying all the characteristics of the Dharma.
All worthy sages and celestial kings will rejoice.
If one performs the rites of the fundamental mudrās and fundamental mantras,
one should in all cases perform the invocation and the boundary-binding.
His coming and going resembled that of a king, and his movements and deportment were no different from his majestic bearing.
Next, form the mudrā of incense and flowers:
cross the two ring fingers and the two little fingers.
Press the right hand over the left within the palms;
then bend them toward the wrists and extend the tips of the middle fingers so that they touch each other at an angle.
With the two index fingers, pinch the third joints of the middle fingers respectively.
With the two thumbs, place them against the sides of the two index fingers and join the wrists.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ maṇārathe parigrahye svāhā. Whether one constructs a maṇḍala at the site or does not construct a maṇḍala.
In a place facing an empty space,
or if there is a consecrated altar site,
perform the ritual of mantra, mudrā, and maṇḍala.
Consecrate incense and flowers and enter the maṇḍala to make offerings. Even if there is no maṇḍala,
it is also permissible to perform the ritual mudrās and offerings while facing an image in an empty space.
First, there should be incense and flowers upon the altar.
All the celestial kings, benevolent deities, and vajras will rejoice.
Next, perform the mudrā of food and drink.
Following the previous mudrā for incense and flowers,
change only the two little fingers and the two ring fingers,
placing them against the center of the palms.
The mantra is:
Namaḥ jaye te pāpasa-rāte tātata-tara-ta nara-yañ-ja-pa-svāhā. This is the mudrā and the mantra.
If one intends to offer food and drink as an act of worship,
one should consecrate each food tray with a mantra;
once the consecration of each has been completed with its respective mantra, [the offering may proceed].
Thereafter, enter the maṇḍala site and arrange the offerings;
if there is no food or drink, [proceed as follows].
However, even if one merely forms the mudrā and recites the mantra before the image of the Heavenly King every morning as an offering, one will likewise obtain blessings and merit;
the Heavenly King will be pleased.
Next, form the mudrā of the lamp:
bend the little finger and ring finger of the right hand into the palm,
and extend the middle finger straight upward.
The index finger is also bent toward the palm;
the thumb is bent at its upper joint,
pressing down upon the upper joint of the index finger.
Press the side of the thumb against the middle joint of the middle finger.
The mantra is:
Oṃ bheṭi le svāhā. If there is a maṇḍala, [perform this].
One must empower the lamps using the mudrā and mantra before entering the maṇḍala to perform offerings.
If there is no maṇḍala,
place an image of the Heavenly King in a clean, empty room.
One must also empower the lamp mudrā and recite the mantra as an offering;
through this spiritual power, the radiance will illuminate the destination without obstruction,
and the Heavenly King will rejoice.
For the mudrā of the Four Heavenly Kings’ boundary-binding: with both hands, tuck the little fingers into the palms;
press the right hand over the left;
and extend the middle and ring fingers upright, leaving them one inch apart.
Place the two index fingers against the two thumbs,
bending them both into the palms.
The mantra is as follows:
Recite "Ha" and bind this seal once more to demarcate the boundary.
Stamp it three times each on the upper and lower parts;
all malevolent māras will be dispersed far away.
Then, marking the four directions—east, west, south, and north—in a continuous cycle, one forms the mudrās and recites the mantras to empower them;
all obstructing māras will flee and dare not approach the maṇḍala.
Having bound the boundary three times, four times, and repeatedly according to the ritual,
one may then invoke the Heavenly King; thus,
the power of accomplishment will be attained.
One immediately attains fearlessness.
Next, perform the mudrā for summoning and invitation:
grasp the left wrist with the right hand held forward.
At the crown of the head, move the four fingers of the left hand back and forth.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ vairocanāya samantabhūmivikrāmiṇe svāhā*. Perform this mudrā and recite the mantra seven times.
The retinue of the Heavenly King descended upon the ritual assembly.
He spoke, saying:
"Out of compassion, Heavenly King, please take your seat and accept this small offering."
Having invited his followers to each take their seats to receive his offerings,
he knelt with palms joined and, holding an incense burner in his hands,
stood before the Heavenly King.
With a sincere heart, I respectfully invoke the assemblies of deities, yakṣas, rākṣasas, buddhas, bodhisattvas,
and vīras, to descend upon this ritual site and bear witness for me.
May the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa descend upon this sacred site;
may we achieve the supernatural powers of the Dharma-force and attain great sovereignty.
May all your wishes be fulfilled according to your will.
May you move Heaven and shake the Earth, bringing harmony between ruler and minister.
May the military and the people support one another, and may the populace cherish and care for each other.
All undertakings accord with one's wishes.
If there is divine efficacy, it is not in vain;
the Heavenly King manifests his presence through miraculous transformations.
May I obtain verification of this.
The Great Body Dhāraṇī of the Heavenly King is as follows: *Namaḥ ratnatrāya*.
Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye mahākrodhāya | Nama āhata khaḥ ||
1. *Lū-ṇī bū-ṇī dā-ra-ya* 2. *Dhi-pa-śa-ya* 3.
*Vai-śi-ra-ma-na-va-tsa-nā-sa-ya* 4. *Ma-hā-ra-ja-sa-ya* 5. *Ya-kṣi*
Kṣa dīpa dha sa-ja va-ma ta sa-ja sat-ta ta sa-ja bha-śa-na pra-va-ha-na sa-ja hi-ma-da.
Ṭa ṭa ni prasa yā mi | tadyathā | kuśāmi kuśāmi kuśāmi viśrama mana sāya || 10–13 ||
14. *mā* 15. *raja* 16. *īpandata* 17. *nirmitaromasa* 18. *sarvaha*. If there be anyone who upholds [this],...
Recite the mantra purely three hundred thousand times.
Whatever undertakings you perform under the protective empowerment of the Heavenly King, all thoughts and intentions shall be subdued.
Furthermore, all honors, emoluments, and official positions shall accord with your heart's wishes.
If there is someone who begins on the first or fifteenth day of the month and recites three hundred thousand times,
the one who constructs the altar shall have musical instruments.
If there is even the slightest atom of a mind that follows [me],
I shall always protect it as I would guard my own pupils.
One should protect [the mantra] as one protects one's own life.
If one recites while holding incense in the mouth, both one's own mind and that of others will know it.
If one constantly maintains the recitation of my true mantra without interruption.
I sit and lie down following this person;
I always follow this person in going out and coming in, in departing and returning;
I follow this person so that their wishes and intentions are fulfilled.
If one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times each day,
the sins of one hundred and eight kalpas within one's body will be extinguished.
If one recites and maintains my mantra for ten thousand times, [the same result shall be attained].
It can extinguish the eighty-four thousand grave offenses of the ten evils and the five heinous crimes;
all sins such as destroying stupas, violating the precepts, and filial impiety shall be completely eliminated.
If one stands before the face of the Heavenly King, [these merits shall be realized].
If one recites and maintains the body-mantra one hundred thousand times,
one will also achieve slight success according to one's needs. Furthermore,
if one makes daily offerings to my image, [the results will be even greater].
To those who have offered me mental music and milk-gruel as an offering,
I shall manifest a body clad in golden armor to fulfill their aspirations;
if they blend various fragrances together, [I shall likewise grant their wishes].
Take equal parts of ox-gallstone and cinnabar;
empower them and place them beneath the feet of my image.
I shall grant you the accomplishment of the incense rite according to your wishes; apply [the mixture] to your own forehead.
Wherever he goes, he sees kings, princes, ministers, officials, and various nobles;
all whom he encounters rejoice,
and the soldiers hold him in affection.
If one can, every day at noon,
facing north before the image,
recite my heart-mantra three hundred thousand times.
I manifest in the form of a great general,
appearing before you with halberd and sword in hand;
I manifest my body within your dreams.
Or I may show you from atop a distant mountain peak so that you may see me;
thus all your wishes shall be fulfilled,
even if you do not behold my physical form.
I shall also grant your wish;
I shall bestow my protective empowerment upon you through mindfulness.
The heart-mantra of the Northern Heavenly King is as follows:
Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śaktavajrapāṇaye mahākṣaye ||
Pātāye nāmo ātaḥ kuru yakṣiṇa sarvamamāraṃ jñāna praviśa smaraṇa.
*Vasatvāhiteṣṭānām oṃ maṇivajrāya svāhā | bhrūṇavajrāya svāhā | māṃ*
Naraya svāhā | Śaṅkarāya svāhā | Viśvarūpāya svāhā | Nandikeśvarāya svāhā | If one receives...
For one who maintains the recitation of my heart-mantra and performs various offerings,
my body and mind shall dwell solely upon your person;
I shall love and cherish you immeasurably.
If there are those who seek wealth, seek official rank,
or seek all manner of external worldly matters,
it shall cause your own wishes to be fulfilled.
I shall not allow wicked people to harm you.
Those among you who are able to receive and uphold my Dharma will immediately attain wealth, honor, peace, and happiness.
Handsome men and women, male and female slaves, vehicles, the five grains, beans, wheat, fields and estates, and wives and concubines—
I shall certainly bestow these upon you all,
providing every means for your enjoyment.
Your wishes shall be fulfilled.
Until the end of your life, wherever you are reborn,
your place of birth shall not conflict with your aspirations.
If this is not true,
I shall not be called the Heavenly King who Protects the Dharma;
I shall surely fall into the Avīci Hell for your sake.
"You who receive, uphold, read, and recite [this],
yet give rise to even a slight doubt within my Dharma, slandering and reviling it—
all of you have not yet exhausted the causal conditions for the suffering of hell."
Know then that there will be no time of deliverance for this person.
You people who wish to maintain [this practice] should prepare incense,
flowers, oil, ghee, and lamps, and establish a water-mandala, placing the image within it.
Various kinds of grasses, fruits, foods, drinks, fried cakes, milk products, curds, and the like,
as well as bowls of gruel, clarified butter, and honey, were offered according to the ritual.
Music was performed and hymns were chanted.
Praise with a Brahma-like voice.
In this manner, perform recitation and circumambulation daily, on the first and fifteenth days of each month, and on the seventh day of the first month, before the image.
I shall manifest my body;
or I will bestow various precious objects within the maṇḍala to satisfy you,
or I will act according to your heart's desire.
To whatever places you may go— east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions,
above, and below— to all such places, even within your dreams,
we shall bestow [these things] upon you.
It will cause people to enter the fray without fear, where they cannot be harmed by swords or halberds and remain unknown to others.
You need only keep my name and the phrases of the mantra in mind,
while holding the ritual mudrā in your hand.
All the evil enemy soldiers and bandits in the direction one intends [to face] shall all bind themselves,
scatter themselves, fall into confusion, perish themselves, and go mad themselves.
There is none who can harm my Dharma.
If there is anyone who holds my heart-mantra,
they should mix fragrant incense and hold it in their mouth when seeing a person of noble rank.
Take musk, saffron, camphor, cloves, and so forth,
and combine them in whatever quantities are appropriate.
Place the mixture in a casket made of gold or silver.
If there is no casket made of gold or silver,
use a casket made of white lapis lazuli;
if there is no casket made of lapis lazuli...
A porcelain casket is used to contain blended incense.
This is from the *Separate Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Sublime Dhāraṇī of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of Abundant Treasures*, Year 2 of the Enpō era.
He was commissioned to transcribe it.
On the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month in the sixth year of the Genroku era,
the clean transcription and collation were completed.
May this most rare and secret wheel turn perpetually throughout the worlds of sand-grains, so that all may be moistened by the Dharma rain;
may the Buddha-sun shine forever,
and may the multitudes of sentient beings all receive its compassionate light.
Recorded by the Ācārya Jingyan, who received the Vajra Secret Precepts and transmitted the Yoga Vehicle at the inaugural ceremony of Lingyun in the Northern Suburb of the Eastern Capital.
